newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Cimpor sees no further buys short-term. [CORRECTED 17:30 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Cimpor sees no further buys short-term. [CORRECTED 17:30 GMT]

text.p: Portuguese cement firm Cimpor said that it had no plans for further company purchases in the short-term, preferring to concentrate on integrating recent acquisitions.
"Unless the conditions were exceptionally attractive, no further purchases are expected," chairman Antonio Sousa Gomes told a news conference called to present the 1996 results.
Earlier this year, the company bought two Brazilian cement concerns -- Cisafra and the cement operations of the Serrana group.
Sousa Gomes said that the company would continue to focus on its areas of strategic interest -- North Africa, Latin America and Europe.
Cement sales rose 6.6 percent to 4.96 million tonnes in 1996, giving the company 60 percent of the Portuguese market. Sales fell (corrects from rose) 7.5 percent to 1.13 million tonnes in Spain.
